approach: Set typography through the same mat.theme mixin used for color — either by name (a font family string) for Material's default M3 sizes/weights, or with a config map for per-role font family and weight control.
explanation: Passing a bare string (e.g. typography: Roboto) to mat.theme sets every Material type role to that one font family at Material's default M3 sizes/weights. Passing a map instead lets you set the font family (and optionally per-role weight) without touching the size/line-height defaults, which are already tuned to the M3 spec. Angular Material only emits typography-related CSS custom properties (--mat-sys-*) — loading the actual font file (a Google Fonts <link>, a self-hosted @font-face, etc.) is your responsibility, exactly as in a plain CSS project.
gotchas: Setting typography via mat.theme does not load the font file — forgetting the accompanying <link>/@font-face means every component silently falls back to the browser's default sans-serif rather than erroring.

The per-role type scale (display/headline/title/body/label, each in large/medium/small) is derived from M3 defaults and isn't part of the simplified typography map — use the lower-level typography-level mixins if you need to override individual role sizes rather than just family/weights.

A typography map applies globally to every Material component reading the shared --mat-sys-* tokens; scoping a different typeface to one section of the app means re-including mat.theme (or just its typography portion) inside that section's own selector, not overriding font-family in plain CSS after the fact.
